prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale: Earth-observation mission (land/coastal/cryosphere imaging). Ground segment plans, acquires, operates, processes, archives, gives access; spacecraft, launch, external user processing outside. Elements: Mission Control Center (MCC, alias Bluebell): real-time ops, pass supervision, anomaly response, releases validated commands, owns contact schedule, hosts primary routing policy point. Flight Dynamics Facility (alias Mistral): orbit, maneuvers, navigation; sends visibility predictions and antenna pointing products to planning. Payload Processing Facility: processing, calibration, distribution staging; coordinates Primary (nominal)/Backup (failover) Processing Clusters on downlink changes. Network Control System (alias Lantern): authoritative wide area circuit status (circuit state, path selection, maintenance windows); distributes station allocations, confirms antenna readiness, records actual contact times. Mission Planning System: receives contact booking requests (service type, antenna preference, min elevation, data volume, priority). Command Validation Gateway: rule-checks plans. Telemetry Ingest Service: receives telemetry, contact status, data-flow indicators; feeds ops/engineering/processing. Orbit Determination Engine: produces Doppler Residual Report per qualified pass. Product Quality Service; Long Term Archive; User Services Portal. Antennas: North S-Band (nominal uplink), South S-Band (alternate) connect to MCC via protected access routers separating command/telemetry from admin traffic; Kiruna X-Band, Svalbard X-Band (high-rate) use dual WAN paths to Payload Processing Facility surviving single carrier outage. Redundant terrestrial circuits link MCC, FDF, PPF, Archive. Actors: Ground Network Manager (alias Juniper): antenna readiness, conflict arbitration, Antenna Deicing Notice, pins critical paths before AOS if maintenance risks route oscillation. Spacecraft Ops, Flight Dynamics, Payload Calibration Teams; Cybersecurity Desk; local station teams notify MCC of constraints. Rules: daily cut-off freezes routine contacts; later contingency needs justification. Priority: safety, timeliness, efficiency. Weather degrades X/S-band. Human command authorization. Antenna performance trends reviewed for corrective actions. Routing: approved prefixes, authenticated neighbors, deterministic preferences, no ad hoc changes; dynamic routing only on controlled adjacencies; static backups for unpredictable sites; management access on unadvertised admin networks. Latency budgets per service class; MCC-CVG-TIS real-time budget end-to-end incl. encryption/firewall; ODE traffic tighter jitter.

New part:
S065: Transfers from the Primary Processing Cluster to the Long Term Archive are rate limited during active contacts so that bulk movement cannot starve operational telemetry or control-plane monitoring.
S066: The Backup Processing Cluster receives lower routing preference during normal operations, but its paths are tested routinely so that failover does not expose stale firewall rules or asymmetric return routes.
S067: If a latency budget is exceeded, the Ground Network Manager first verifies carrier performance, then checks routing state, packet loss, queue depth, and security inspection delays before declaring a mission-impacting network condition.
S068: Time synchronization is provided from redundant reference clocks at the Mission Control Center and the Flight Dynamics Facility, with holdover capability sized to cover credible external timing outages.
S069: Precision Time Protocol is used inside data centers and processing enclaves where sub-millisecond alignment is required for correlation, while authenticated Network Time Protocol is used for general server and workstation timekeeping.
S070: Antenna site equipment validates time against independent local references before contact start so that tracking records, telemetry frames, and operator displays remain comparable across locations.
S071: The Flight Dynamics Team monitors timing quality alongside orbit support metrics because clock bias can appear as an apparent measurement error if it is not separated from actual tracking performance.
S072: Timing alarms are forwarded to the Spacecraft Operations Team only after the Network Control System confirms that the alarm is not caused by a known maintenance interval or a failed local reference check.
S073: Cybersecurity monitoring is applied at each site through network sensors, endpoint telemetry, privileged-access logging, and configuration compliance checks that are reviewed during every operational shift.
S074: The Cybersecurity Desk sends a Security Exception Ticket when a monitored event requires temporary deviation from the approved security baseline.
S075: Correlation rules emphasize changes that could affect mission continuity, including unexpected route advertisements, repeated authentication failures, unscheduled remote access, and unexplained increases in encrypted traffic volume.
S076: During contingency operations, the Ground Network Manager and the Cybersecurity Desk coordinate before blocking traffic so that protective actions do not unintentionally interrupt a spacecraft contact or prevent recovery of processing services.
S077: Following the network coordination described in the preceding section, the Mission Control Center treats every scheduled contact as a controlled operational activity with a defined readiness check, live monitoring period, and post-pass closure step.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
